subject: Use empty facet space and place another plot

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Use empty facet space and place another plot
parts:
Hello all,

I have a question about utilizing the space created when you have an
odd number of facets but an even number of facet columns like so:

##
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width))+
geom_point() +
facet_wrap(~Species, ncol=2)
##


For example, if this were spatial data it might be useful to have a
map in the white space area. I've found plenty of example to embed a
plot with a single plot but they don't seem to apply to this case. My
particular confusion is that I don't really know the set of
coordinates that I need to use to palce the plot outside of the
facetted area.

Thanks in advance!

Sam

messages.author: 62055bacc3ed4f0b
messages.subject: Re: Use empty facet space and place another plot
parts:
I needed to overlay two plots yesterday and found the library wq, which lets you specify a grid and place plots wherever you want on the grid, including overlapping. You might need to play with it a little to get the effect you want, but here's an example:

##
library(ggplot2) 
library(wq)
p1 <- ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width))+ 
  geom_point() + 
  facet_wrap(~Species, ncol=2) 

p2 <- ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length))+ 
  geom_bar()  
  
layOut(list(p1, 1:2,1:2), list(p2, 2:2,2:2))
##

Regards,
Bonnie
